audit_findings.title: Recurring acquisitions may be omitted while acquired-intangible amortization is added back
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 acquired-intangible amortization was $199.2 million, equal to 61.3% of the $324.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is overstated if acquired-intangible amortization is added back without deducting the recurring acquisition expenditure necessary to replace acquired products, technology and customer relationships.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate an acquisition-dependent business model and material amortization, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation added back the $199.2 million while omitting maintenance acquisition spending. The potential asymmetry is large relative to the anchor and could materially change normalized OE and every scenario value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year from reported cash flow to calculated OE, identify all amortization add-backs, tabulate acquisition and installment cash payments, classify maintenance versus expansion transactions, and rerun the valuation with any demonstrated maintenance-acquisition charge.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may perpetuate a temporarily hedged, pre-refinancing interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 included $36.1 million of swap gains, equal to 11.1% of the OE anchor, while the April 2026 filing shows $950.0 million extended to 2031 and $550.0 million still maturing in December 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the DCF uses equity-level OE, any understatement of normalized after-tax interest directly overstates the OE anchor and its projected growth path.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2021 Credit Agreement provides for a term loan facility (the 2021 Term Loan Facility) in an aggregate principal amount of $ 1,500.0 million, which, unless terminated earlier, matures on December 17, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The hedge benefit is presently embedded in reported interest expense, but its enduring effect is unresolved. The latest filing narrows the original refinancing concern because $950.0 million was extended, although $550.0 million still requires resolution and $1.3 billion of swaps had less than two years remaining. Future rates, refinancing spreads and replacement hedges are not established, so the record cannot quantify the normalized interest adjustment or establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Build a debt-by-debt after-tax interest schedule using the February 2026 amendment, the $550.0 million maturity, the five surviving swaps and their expiration dates; rerun OE under documented refinancing-rate and hedge-rolloff assumptions.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may double count customer-funded cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum bridge exposure of $138.8 million, or $0.69 per share; April 2026 deferred revenue was $336.7 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any customer-funded portion of cash that is required to satisfy prepaid storage obligations should be reserved in the equity bridge rather than added as unrestricted excess cash while the related future revenue remains in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred revenue primarily represents prepaid stem cell storage as part of the CooperSurgical business unit.
audit_findings.explanation: The customer-funded portion is unresolved, but the valuation can overstate equity by no more than the entire $138.8 million cash add-back. Removing all of it would reduce base value from $23.44 to approximately $22.75 per share, still far below the $69.59 market price; therefore this bridge issue cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace cash receipts from prepaid storage contracts, quantify future service costs and unrestricted excess cash, and deduct only the demonstrated customer-funded reserve in a bridge sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Gross option shares do not match the equity numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum denominator correction of 3.487729 million shares, 1.74% of the 200.63149 million-share denominator; excluding every option would increase scenario values by at most approximately $0.46 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Counting options as full shares without recognizing exercise proceeds overstates the diluted share denominator and understates per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: We determine diluted EPS by increasing the weighted-average number of shares outstanding in the denominator by the number of outstanding dilutive equity awards using the treasury stock method.
audit_findings.explanation: The numerator-denominator inconsistency is demonstrated. Its maximum possible correction is nevertheless small: even assuming none of the 3.487729 million options dilutes, base value rises only to approximately $23.86 and bull value to approximately $26.56 per share, both far below $69.59.
audit_findings.action: Replace gross option shares with option-by-option treasury-stock or fair-value dilution using strike prices and remaining lives, while retaining separate gross or probability-weighted treatment for no-strike RSUs and PSUs.

audit_findings.title: A transition-tax claim may be missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum unresolved amount of $36.9 million, or approximately $0.18 per share, based on the October 2025 filed balance
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid transition-tax liability is a claim ahead of common equity and should be deducted in the bridge because its payment does not recur through projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The remaining transition tax to be remitted from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 is $ 36.9 million as of October 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the liability remained unpaid at April 2026 is unresolved, but even deducting the entire October 2025 balance would reduce base value only from $23.44 to approximately $23.26 per share, less than 1% of base equity value and immaterial to the conclusion relative to the $69.59 market price.
audit_findings.action: Verify the transition-tax balance and payments through April 30, 2026 from the tax-liability roll-forward, payment records or supporting 10-Q detail, then deduct any confirmed unpaid balance.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may capitalize a restructuring trough
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed FY2025 termination-benefit expense was $35.0 million, equal to 10.8% of the $324.9 million OE anchor, with related write-offs not separately quantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining genuinely exceptional restructuring charges understates normalized OE, while adding back costs that recur through ongoing optimization and obsolescence overstates OE and value.
audit_findings.evidence: We recognized termination benefits expense of $ 35.0 million associated with the workforce optimization initiatives in fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The severance charge is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether it remained in OE, its tax-effected OE impact, the amount of associated inventory and long-lived-asset write-offs, or whether such costs are exceptional. The possible direction therefore depends on recurrence and existing OE treatment, and materiality cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $35.0 million severance and each related write-off to FY2025 OE, review comparable charges across the historical OE period, classify exceptional versus recurring costs, and rerun the anchor only for demonstrated nonrecurring after-tax amounts.
